translations.1: Then God spoke to Moses in [divine] speech.
translations.2: Command the sons of Israel and say to them: any person who has vowed a vow of souls to God —
translations.3: the valuation of the male, from twenty years of age to sixty years of age, shall be fifty mithqals of silver by the mithqal of the sanctuary;
translations.4: and if it be a female, her valuation shall be thirty;
translations.5: and if it be from five years of age to twenty years of age, the valuation of the male shall be twenty mithqals, and the female ten;
translations.6: and if it be from one month of age to five years of age, the valuation of the male shall be five mithqals of silver, and the female three;
translations.7: and if it be from sixty years of age and upward, the valuation of the male shall be fifteen mithqals, and the female ten;
translations.8: and if he be too lowly for the valuation, he shall stand before the imām, and the imām shall value him according to what the hand of the one who vowed can reach — thus shall the imām value him.
translations.9: And if it be a beast from which an offering may be brought near to God, then everything they designate of it for God shall itself be sacred.
translations.10: He shall not exchange it nor substitute it — good for inferior, nor inferior for good; and if he does substitute one beast for another, then both it and its substitute shall become sacred.
translations.11: And if it be an impure beast, or one from which no offering may be brought near to God, it shall be set before the imām;
translations.12: and the imām shall value it according to its quality, whether good or inferior — as the imām values it, so shall it be obligatory.
translations.13: And if he wishes to redeem it, he shall add a fifth of the valuation to it.
translations.14: And whatever man consecrates his house as sacred to God, the imām shall value it according to its quality, whether good or inferior — as he values it, so shall it be obligatory.
translations.15: And if the one who consecrated it wishes to redeem his dwelling, he shall add a fifth to its valuation, and it shall be his.
translations.16: And if a person consecrates to God something from the fields of his holding, the valuation shall be according to the measure of its seed — every unit sown of barley at fifty mithqals of silver.
translations.17: And if he consecrates his field from the year of release, the valuation shall remain fixed as it is.
translations.18: But if he consecrates it after the year of release, the imām shall reckon for him the silver according to the number of years remaining until the year of release, and it shall be deducted from the full valuation.
translations.19: And if the man who consecrated the field wishes to redeem it, he shall add a fifth to the valuation, and it shall be secured to him.
translations.20: But if he does not redeem it, and the trustee has sold it to another man, it shall not be redeemed ever.
translations.21: And it shall be, upon its passing out of the purchaser's hand in the year of release, sacred to God — like the lands of the endowments irrevocably devoted — and it shall become the imām's.
translations.22: And if a person consecrates a field he has purchased, which is not his by right of holding —
translations.23: the imām shall reckon for him the installments of the valuation from its year until the year of release, and he shall pay it on that day as sacred to God.
translations.24: And the field shall revert in the year of release to the seller from whom he purchased it — to the one who holds title to the land.
translations.25: And all your valuations shall be by the mithqal of the sanctuary — every mithqal being twenty dāniqs.
translations.26: As for a firstborn animal that is made firstborn to God from among the beasts, a person need not consecrate it: whether it be from the cattle or from the flock, it already belongs to God.
translations.27: And if one consecrates something from the impure beasts, he shall redeem it at its valuation and add a fifth to it; and if he does not redeem it, it shall be sold at its valuation.
translations.28: But every irrevocable devotion that a person makes to God from all that he has — whether slaves, or beasts, or the fields of his holding — shall not be sold and shall not be redeemed; it shall be of the most sacred consecrations to God.
translations.29: And every person condemned to destruction who has deserved destruction shall not be redeemed — he shall be put to death.
translations.30: And all the tithes of the land — from its grain and from the fruit of the tree — they belong to God as sacred.
translations.31: And if a person redeems any of his tithe, he shall add a fifth of its value to it.
translations.32: And all the tithes of cattle and of the flock — whatever passes under the staff — the tenth shall be sacred to God.
translations.33: He shall not examine it as between good and inferior, nor shall he substitute it; and if he does substitute it, then both it and its substitute shall become sacred and shall not be redeemed.
translations.34: These are the commandments which God charged Moses with, to the sons of Israel at Mount Sinai.
